chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-Ila' (solemn oath of abstention), what is it? He said: It is when a man says to his wife, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' and he says, 'By Allah, I shall keep you in suspense (by withholding intimacy).' So she is awaited for four months, then he is seized and held. If he returns (reconciles), and it is that he makes peace with his wife, then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce her, and a divorce does not take effect between them, even if it be after the four months, provided he does not refer the matter to the Imam.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ: Four months (the waiting period for Ila')
key_terms.إِلَى الْإِمَامِ: To the Imam (referral for judicial decision)
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Solemn oath of abstention from sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a husband who swears to abstain from his wife (Ila')?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudence of 'al-Ila'', detailing the four-month waiting period and the distinction between voluntary reconciliation and compelled divorce. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that if the husband persists in his oath, he is forced to divorce, yet the divorce does not count as one of the three revocable divorces unless referred to the Imam, preserving the wife's marital status. This mechanism underscores the balance between the husband's vow and the wife's right to resolution, reflecting the practical application of Quranic injunctions in family law.
